motif.name: Power of the Ring
motif.description: Passages of the piano score that match one melody, in levels by how close they are to it. Level 1 is the closest. A run of repeated notes counts as one note. Passages that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other, are joined into one; the level is that of the closest.

source.author: J. K. Holman
source.title: Wagner's Ring: A Listener's Companion & Concordance
source.publication: Portland, Oregon: Amadeus Press, 1996; paperback 2003, ISBN 978-1-57467-070-7

levels.label: Original
levels.name: The melody as given
levels.description: The melody as you gave it. It is not a passage of the score.

levels.name: Closest to the original
levels.description: The best partial matches of the whole phrase. The pitches and the rhythm are the same, in any octave.

levels.name: Same core pitches
levels.description: Notes 1 to 10 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, but the rhythm differs. In a sung passage the score may have one short extra note between two of them: it is skipped.

levels.name: One note different
levels.description: Notes 1 to 10 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, except one note. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Other keys
levels.description: Notes 1 to 10 of the phrase have the same intervals, moved to another key, in any octave. The rhythm may differ.

levels.name: Opening, other keys
levels.description: Only the first notes, 1 to 8 of the phrase, have the same intervals, moved to another key. The rhythm may differ. Short cells also match by chance, so some of these passages are coincidences.

occurrences.label: The original
occurrences.note: The melody as you gave it, engraved from your notes. It has no pickup, the bars are in 3/4, and the score has a treble clef and 5 flats in the key signature. It is not a passage of the score.

occurrences.label: Closest match: 9 of 10 notes, joined with 1 more
occurrences.note: Your notes 1 to 9 (of 10) match in pitch and rhythm. After them, the score has F of 7 eighth notes; yours has A of 6 eighth notes. This joins 2 passages (levels 1, 3) that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other.
